name: Grill Me
description: Systematically interrogate the user's mental model of a proposed codebase change using a design tree, before planning begins. Surfaces assumptions, constraints and expectations the initial description leaves out, and persists them as a machine-readable tree plus a human-readable handoff summary.

tested_contexts: Interactive Claude Code CLI sessions run immediately before a planning session, on the author's own small-to-medium single-repo codebases

Projects carrying an Open Knowledge Format vault, where both the vault-reading path (prior decisions sharpening questions) and the vault-emission path (settled decisions written back as notes) were exercised
boundaries: Not tested on large monorepos, where reading the code before each question becomes expensive enough to change the questioning cadence
Not tested in headless or non-interactive runs — the design tree only advances on turn-by-turn answers from a human
Not tested against knowledge vaults in any format other than Open Knowledge Format, and the vault-emission path is skipped entirely when the open-knowledge-format skill is absent
Not tested on client delivery codebases, or with any user other than the author, so the questioning tone has not been calibrated against unfamiliar teams

artefacts: the design tree JSON written to .grill-me/<slug>-<timestamp>.json
the markdown handoff summary written to .grill-me/<slug>-<timestamp>-summary.md
any knowledge vault notes emitted for settled decisions, which the skill must ask before writing
the proposed .gitignore entry for .grill-me/, which the skill must ask before adding
